LOOP ITERATION 8 — J10 IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED (Gerrit change 1103), awaiting LLM-Review +1 and
Verified +1.

THE SPLIT VALIDATED ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: this plan PASSED review on the FIRST round, 0 blocking. J9
had blocked EIGHT times — same author, same session, same subject matter. The difference was one
concern per plan. Recording that because it is the transferable lesson: when a plan keeps returning
double-digit findings, the signal is usually structural (it is carrying two concerns that contradict
each other), not that the wording needs another pass.

RED-first, held out: I wrote 11 tests covering the contract; the implementation subagent was given
ONLY the happy path (a DC 404 must surface as BackendHTTPError with .code == 404). RED was 6 failed /
5 passed — the 5 passers were the Cloud negative controls and the structural no-vendor-exception
checks, which is what proves they are not vacuous. All 11 green after.

THE KEYSTONE, and why the tests are shaped as they are: BackendHTTPError SUBCLASSES
urllib.error.HTTPError. That is what makes the core need NO edit — a subclass matches the existing
'except urllib.error.HTTPError' and .code access is preserved by construction. So the decisive tests
drive the REAL core functions (outbound_differ._safe_get_issue, dispatch_apply_phases.
_update_one_apply_reporter) rather than re-implementing their logic. An isinstance-only test would
have passed even if the classification it exists to protect had broken.

Held-out edges that a happy-path-only implementation could have failed:
 * a DC non-404 (403/500/503) must be _TRANSPORT_ERROR, NOT _DELETED. Mapping every DC failure to
   _DELETED would be far worse than the original bug — the reconciler would treat a transient 500 as
   'the issue is gone'.
 * Cloud negative controls on BOTH paths, proving the live-validated Cloud path was not altered
   (brainstorm decision 7).
 * a structural assertion that 'JIRAError' appears in NO core module — if it did, the
   adapter-boundary translation had been abandoned for the very leak this story closes.

Implementation note worth keeping: translation went in at the single choke point every DC transport
method already routes through (_with_connection_retry), so there is no per-method plumbing and the
retry/TLS policy is untouched. The two in-file JIRAError handlers now catch the translated type, so
the vendor name left the file entirely.

VERIFIED: 1660 reconciler unit tests pass, make lint 0, make typecheck 0 (399 files), module-size gate
clean. Next: gates on 1103, submit, close J10 — which UNBLOCKS J9.
